summary: The National Scholarship Programme (NSP) of the Slovak Republic supports mobility stays of foreign master's students, PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists at Slovak higher education and research institutions. It is funded by the Slovak Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth and administered by SAIA, n. o. It pays a monthly amount toward living costs in Slovakia and, for students and PhD students, a travel grant. It does not fund full degree studies in Slovakia.
eligibility_notes:
Citizens of any country except Slovakia can apply.

Category A, students: you must be a university student abroad at master's level, or have completed at least 2.5 years of the same or a similar programme by the deadline, and you must be accepted by a Slovak public, private or state higher education institution for an academic mobility stay. All conditions apply. Doctoral students are not in this category. Stay length: 1 to 2 full semesters (4-5 or 9-10 months), or 1 to 3 full trimesters (3-4, 6-7 or 9-10 months) where the year is split into trimesters.

Category B, PhD students: you must study or research outside Slovakia and be accepted by a Slovak higher education or research institution authorised to run doctoral programmes (for example the Slovak Academy of Sciences). Stay length: 1 to 10 months.

Category C, university teachers, researchers and artists: you must be invited by a Slovak institution that holds a valid R&D eligibility certificate and is not a business company. Stay length: 1 to 10 months.

A stay of at least one month must cover one full calendar month (for example 5 March to 4 April); the same logic applies to other month minimums.

Not supported: full degree study in Slovakia (or people already enrolled in full degree study there); teachers, researchers and artists without a PhD or equivalent who have more than 4 years of experience (PhD studies count as experience), with possible exceptions for 4 to 7 years of experience at the lowest rate only; applicants who spent 15 or more months in Slovakia in the 36 months before the deadline; and applicants accepted under another publicly funded programme for the same stay, such as the International Visegrad Fund, Erasmus+, CEEPUS or bilateral agreements (double funding).

Re-applying: at least 2 years must pass between the deadline you re-apply under and the deadline under which your last NSP scholarship was awarded and received, with exceptions for special cases, especially force majeure.

The host letter must not mention acceptance under another scholarship programme or admission to full degree studies in Slovakia; such letters fail the formal check.
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated for students or PhD students. For teachers, researchers and artists, the monthly amount depends on experience counted up to the application deadline (PhD studies count, up to 6 years). Without a PhD and with more than 4 years of experience: not supported, with limited exceptions for 4 to 7 years at the lowest rate.
funding_summary: A monthly scholarship toward living costs in Slovakia (food, accommodation and similar), for the length of the approved stay of 1 to 10 months depending on category. Students and PhD students can also receive a lump-sum travel grant based on distance. Public health insurance is free for holders on stays longer than one month if they live in Slovakia and are not otherwise insured, and a medical confirmation for the residence permit can be reimbursed up to EUR 250. Tuition for full degree studies is not funded.
programmes_note: No field restriction is stated. You propose your own study, research, teaching or artistic programme with the Slovak host (students are advised to list courses and credits, about 30 credits per semester). This is a mobility stay, not a degree programme.
institutions_note: Any Slovak higher education institution (public, private or state), Slovak Academy of Sciences institutes and other eligible institutions under the programme terms. You choose the host and must get its acceptance or invitation letter; the application form has a dropdown of official Slovak institution names.

summary.detail: Category A (students): master's-level students, or students with at least 2.5 years of the same or a similar programme completed by the deadline, studying abroad and accepted by a Slovak higher education institution for a 1-2 semester (or 1-3 trimester) mobility stay. Monthly amount EUR 620; travel grant by distance.

Category B (PhD students): doctoral students studying or researching outside Slovakia, accepted by a Slovak institution authorised to run doctoral programmes. Stay of 1 to 10 months. Monthly amount EUR 1,025.50; travel grant by distance.

Category C covers university teachers, researchers and artists invited by a Slovak institution, for 1 to 10 months. The page does not use the word postdoctoral; amounts depend on whether the person holds a PhD and on years of experience (EUR 1,025.50, 1,370 or 1,470 per month). No travel grant for this category.
summary.source_text: C) University teachers, researchers and artists

benefits.limit_text: Per month: EUR 620 (master's-level student); EUR 1,025.50 (PhD student); EUR 1,025.50 (teacher, researcher or artist without a PhD, under 4 years of experience); EUR 1,370 (with PhD, under 10 years of experience); EUR 1,470 (with PhD, over 10 years of experience)
benefits.conditions: Meant to cover living costs in Slovakia such as food and accommodation. Paid monthly to a bank account (preferably in a SEPA country), starting after SAIA has the bank details and confirmation that the stay began. The host institution may help with accommodation, or you arrange it yourself.

benefits.limit_text: Lump-sum travel grant by straight-line distance from home address or home institution to the host: up to 200 km EUR 0; over 200 to 300 km EUR 50; over 300 to 500 km EUR 100; over 500 to 1,000 km EUR 250; over 1,000 to 2,000 km EUR 350; over 2,000 to 3,000 km EUR 500; over 3,000 to 5,000 km EUR 750; over 5,000 to 7,000 km EUR 1,100; over 7,000 km EUR 1,500
benefits.conditions: Students and PhD students only (not teachers, researchers or artists). Must be requested with the application. Paid with the final scholarship payment. SAIA recommends the European Commission Erasmus+ distance calculator but may use other methods.

benefits.limit_text: Free public health insurance for scholarship holders staying in Slovakia longer than one month; reimbursement of up to EUR 250 for the medical examination and certificate
benefits.conditions: Public insurance: for foreign holders living in Slovakia who are not otherwise insured; apply with the chosen insurer, whose process may differ. The EUR 250 reimbursement applies to non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens staying over 90 days who need a temporary residence permit and must give the foreign police a health confirmation within 30 days of the permit; send the original medical bill to SAIA before the final-report deadline.

benefits.limit_text: Full degree study in Slovakia is not supported
benefits.conditions: The programme funds mobility stays only; students already enrolled in full degree study in Slovakia are not supported.

benefits.limit_text: Visa and residence costs are not described as covered
benefits.conditions: The visa page lists a national visa fee of EUR 50 for scholarship holders and EUR 90 for a visa used for a residence permit application in Slovakia; the residence card costs EUR 10 or EUR 39, and the application fee may be waived for scholarship holders. Visa centres may add a service fee.

requirements.text: Curriculum vitae with personal information, education, work experience and skills. Use points or short paragraphs, not full sentences; the Europass format is recommended.

Motivation letter: why you want the stay, your goals, how it helps your career and why you chose this Slovak host. Students mention academic and extra-academic activities. PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists link the stay to their dissertation or work and say how they will use the results after returning home.
requirements.conditional_rule: Students and PhD students (not listed for teachers, researchers and artists)

requirements.text: Detailed programme of the stay: activities, goals, host institution name, duration, start and end dates. Students list courses and credits agreed with the home institution (about 30 ECTS credits per semester; justify any deviation). PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists should add a time plan with phases.

Recommendation letters on the home institution's letterhead, signed, with the author's full name, address and position, each different and not older than 3 months at the deadline. Students: two letters from university teachers. PhD students: one letter from the dissertation supervisor.
requirements.conditional_rule: Students (two letters) and PhD students (one letter); not listed for category C

requirements.text: Official confirmation of regular student or PhD status from the home institution, not older than 3 months, stating year of study, standard length of study and expected completion date. A declaration of honour may be used under force majeure, with the official confirmation required before an award.

Students: bachelor's diploma, diploma supplement and state examination certificate if applicable. PhD students: master's diploma, supplement and state examination certificate if applicable. Teachers, researchers and artists: diploma of the highest academic degree achieved.

Acceptance or invitation letter from the Slovak host institution on letterhead, signed, in Slovak or English (matching the application language), not older than 3 months, stating the exact stay period. A scan is uploaded with the application and the original must reach SAIA in Bratislava by 12:00 on the 3rd working day after the deadline. It must not mention another scholarship or admission to full degree study. For PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists it should show real host interest and describe planned activities.
List of publications (or artistic activities) in the prescribed form, or a statement that there are none; other formats fail the formal check.
requirements.conditional_rule: PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists

requirements.text: Transcript or proof of exams passed during the earlier stay.
requirements.conditional_rule: Students who previously held an NSP student scholarship

requirements.text: Documents in languages other than Slovak or English need the original plus an official Slovak or English translation (Czech needs none). Third-party documents are uploaded as scans; originals must be kept and shown on request. Signatures must be handwritten or officially verifiable electronic signatures.

application_steps.title: Choose a Slovak host and ask for an acceptance or invitation letter
application_steps.detail: Contact the Slovak institution by email or phone, say you want a study, research, teaching or artistic stay and may receive an NSP scholarship, give your programme or research plan, the stay period and the date you need the letter, and send your CV and motivation letter or draft programme. The letter must be in Slovak or English and state the exact stay dates.

application_steps.title: Check the call deadline and stay dates
application_steps.detail: Deadlines are 16:00 CET on 30 April (for stays in the next academic year) and 31 October (for stays in the summer semester of the current academic year). Under the 30 April deadline, student stays start between 1 September and 1 April and end by 31 August; under 31 October they start between 1 February and 1 April. PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists have longer windows (end by 30 November). Only one application per call. As of this check the 31 October 2026 call is shown as closed; no date for the next call is announced.

application_steps.title: Complete the online application and request the travel grant
application_steps.detail: Apply in the SAIA online system in Slovak or English. The system opens at least 6 weeks before each deadline; submit early. Choose the host institution from the dropdown list (use 'Other' only if it is missing). Students and PhD students must request the travel grant with the application. Upload CV, motivation letter, study or research programme, recommendation letters, status confirmation, diploma and host letter scan.

application_steps.title: Make sure the original host letter reaches SAIA
application_steps.detail: The original acceptance or invitation letter must arrive at the SAIA office in Bratislava by 12:00 on the 3rd working day after the deadline. The host institution can send it, but if it fails the effect is the same as if you had failed. A scan must be attached to the online application or it cannot be submitted.

application_steps.title: SAIA formal check
application_steps.detail: On the deadline day SAIA checks the application against the formal rules. It can reject applications with formal defects, inconsistent facts, false completeness declarations, conflicting terms or serious past breaches by former holders (which can bar re-application for 10 years). It may ask for more documents. You are responsible for completeness; corrections after submission are not guaranteed.

application_steps.title: Selection Committee ranks applications; there is no interview
application_steps.detail: A Committee appointed by the Ministry judges the application and attachments only. It looks at the reasons for choosing the host and the programme, how you will use the results, personal and professional qualities, recommendation letters, study or research achievements, feedback from a previous stay, contribution to the host, and overall quality. It ranks by category, sets a quality threshold, considers the budget, may award conditional scholarships (for example a shorter stay) and may keep a reserve list until the next deadline. A scholarship is not guaranteed.

application_steps.title: Wait for results and complain in writing if needed
application_steps.detail: SAIA usually tells applicants the outcome within 8 weeks of the deadline. Complaints go to SAIA in writing within 1 month of publication of the results, with your details, application number and grounds; SAIA usually replies within 1 month.

application_steps.title: Accept the Letter of Award in writing
application_steps.detail: If there is no obstacle, SAIA sends a Letter of Award and binding scholarship offer after receiving the original host letter. A contract exists only when you accept in writing. Before the first payment send the signed acceptance letter (SAIA form), a notarised copy of your highest diploma, and (students and PhD students) an original confirmation of studies valid for the academic year issued no earlier than one month before September (or February for summer-semester stays). Conditional awards are finalised once the conditions are met.

application_steps.title: Arrange visa or residence permit and health cover
application_steps.detail: For stays over 90 days SAIA recommends applying for a national visa (type D) at a Slovak mission before departure, at least 40 days before the start; documents include the host's acceptance letter and the SAIA Letter of Award. Holders staying over one month can apply for free public health insurance with the insurer of their choice. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss holders needing a residence permit submit a health confirmation to the foreign police within 30 days of the permit.

application_steps.title: Follow the approved stay and send reports
application_steps.detail: The host country and institution cannot change. Changes to the start date, shortening or interruption need SAIA approval; extensions are not possible (apply again instead). Stays over 6 months need an interim report. After the stay, send a final report and confirmation of completion; SAIA may withhold up to one monthly payment plus the travel grant until received. Disclose other Slovak state support. For serious breaches or false information SAIA may withdraw and demand repayment.

not_stated: Date of the next call after the 31 October 2026 deadline (the programme terms give 30 April and 31 October as recurring deadlines but no year-specific date for the next call)
Number of scholarships awarded per call
Academic score or language-test minimums (no IELTS/TOEFL requirement found; language comes from the host institution)
Whether teachers, researchers and artists are expected to hold postdoctoral status
Any tuition support, since only mobility stays are covered
